sections.body: This section covers the rules and practices that keep AI assisted research honest, from who counts as an author to whether a cited paper exists at all. In practice, AI is now used to draft manuscripts, suggest references, screen ethics applications and generate figures, and each of those uses creates a paper trail that institutions are still learning to audit. Fact checking has become a live task rather than a formality, because language models can produce citations that look plausible and are entirely invented. Provenance work asks where training data and research images came from, who consented, and whether the record can be traced back to a source. The site itself reflects that emphasis by linking to original papers rather than to a summarising search tool, so a reader can check a claim against the work it came from.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts of this are settled. Journal policies on AI authorship are now common, most agree that a model cannot be an author because it cannot take responsibility, and disclosure requirements are widely stated. Fabricated citations are well documented as a failure mode, and simple checks catch many of them, though not all, especially when a real paper is misdescribed rather than invented. Training data provenance remains the weakest area, since many models do not disclose their corpora and researchers cannot always verify what a model was exposed to. Ethics review with AI assistance is uneven, with some committees using tools for triage and others avoiding them over confidentiality and bias concerns. Image and data provenance has improved through standards and metadata, but detection of manipulated figures is still a manual, expert dependent process that does not scale to the volume of submissions.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages here divide the problem by where integrity tends to break. AI and Authorship deals with credit and accountability, which is the question a reader goes to when a model has contributed text to a paper. Fabricated Citations and Fact Checking covers verification of references, the practical check a reader runs when a source looks too convenient. Training Data and Academic Work sits underneath both, since the legality and ethics of a model's inputs shape what it can be trusted to say about prior literature. Ethics Review with AI Assistance addresses the committee side, including what can and cannot be delegated to a tool during approval. Provenance of Research Images and Data closes the loop on the artefacts themselves, covering how images and datasets are traced, stored and checked. Read together they form a chain from input to output, and each page is the place to go when a specific link in that chain is in question.
